```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

# Read in the saved data (originally pulled with tidyquant::tq_get)
unemp_raw <- read_rds("data/unemp_raw.rds")

# Rename and label regions
unemp <- unemp_raw |>
  rename(unemployment_rate = price) |>
  mutate(
    region = case_when(
      symbol == "UNRATE" ~ "United States",
      symbol == "ORUR"   ~ "Oregon",
      symbol == "CAUR"   ~ "California",
      symbol == "TXUR"   ~ "Texas",
      symbol == "NYUR"   ~ "New York"
    )
  )

# Month-over-month change within each region
unemp <- unemp |>
  arrange(region, date) |>
  group_by(region) |>
  mutate(unemployment_rate_change = unemployment_rate - lag(unemployment_rate)) |>
  ungroup()

# Recent sample: January 2015 onward
unemp_recent <- unemp |>
  filter(date >= as.Date("2015-01-01"))

# Summary tables
unemp_summary <- unemp |>
  group_by(region) |>
  summarize(
    mean_rate = mean(unemployment_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_rate  = min(unemployment_rate,  na.rm = TRUE),
    max_rate  = max(unemployment_rate,  na.rm = TRUE)
  )

unemp_recent_summary <- unemp_recent |>
  group_by(region) |>
  summarize(
    mean_rate = mean(unemployment_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_rate  = min(unemployment_rate,  na.rm = TRUE),
    max_rate  = max(unemployment_rate,  na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Largest monthly changes, full sample
unemp_top_increases <- unemp |> slice_max(unemployment_rate_change, n = 5)
unemp_top_decreases <- unemp |> slice_min(unemployment_rate_change, n = 5)

# Largest monthly changes, excluding 2020
unemp_no_covid <- unemp |> filter(year(date) != 2020)

unemp_top_increases_no_covid <- unemp_no_covid |>
  slice_max(unemployment_rate_change, n = 5)

unemp_top_decreases_no_covid <- unemp_no_covid |>
  slice_min(unemployment_rate_change, n = 5)
```

# 1. Data

This analysis uses monthly unemployment rates from the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis' FRED database (underlying data from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics), downloaded with the `tidyquant` package. It covers five regions: the United States (`UNRATE`), Oregon (`ORUR`), California (`CAUR`), Texas (`TXUR`), and New York (`NYUR`). The data runs from `r format(min(unemp$date), "%B %Y")` to `r format(max(unemp$date), "%B %Y")` and contains `r nrow(unemp)` region-month observations. Each row is one region in one month, with the series code (`symbol`), the `date`, and the unemployment rate in percent (`price` in the raw download, renamed `unemployment_rate`).

```{r}
#| label: read-data
#| echo: false
head(unemp_raw) |>
  kable(caption = "First six rows of the raw data as downloaded from FRED.")
```

# 2. Wrangling

I renamed the value column to `unemployment_rate`, added a `region` label for each series code, and computed the month-over-month change in the rate within each region (`unemployment_rate_change`, in percentage points).

## Summary statistics by region

```{r}
#| label: tbl-summary
unemp_summary |>
  kable(
    digits = 2,
    col.names = c("Region", "Mean rate (%)", "Min rate (%)", "Max rate (%)"),
    caption = "Mean, minimum, and maximum unemployment rate by region over the full sample."
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-recent-summary
unemp_recent_summary |>
  kable(
    digits = 2,
    col.names = c("Region", "Mean rate (%)", "Min rate (%)", "Max rate (%)"),
    caption = "Mean, minimum, and maximum unemployment rate by region, January 2015 onward."
  )
```

## Largest monthly changes, excluding 2020

I excluded all of 2020 so the extreme COVID-19 swings do not dominate the results. The month-over-month changes were computed on the full data before dropping 2020, so the first month after the gap is still measured against the true prior month. Ties are kept, so a table can have more than five rows.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-increases
unemp_top_increases_no_covid |>
  select(region, date, unemployment_rate, unemployment_rate_change) |>
  kable(
    digits = 2,
    col.names = c("Region", "Month", "Rate (%)", "Change (pct. pts.)"),
    caption = "Largest month-over-month increases in the unemployment rate, excluding 2020."
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-decreases
unemp_top_decreases_no_covid |>
  select(region, date, unemployment_rate, unemployment_rate_change) |>
  kable(
    digits = 2,
    col.names = c("Region", "Month", "Rate (%)", "Change (pct. pts.)"),
    caption = "Largest month-over-month decreases in the unemployment rate, excluding 2020."
  )
```

# 3. Visualization

## Unemployment rates over time

```{r}
#| label: fig-lines
ggplot(unemp, aes(x = date, y = unemployment_rate, color = region)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    title = "Regional Unemployment Rates Over Time",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Unemployment Rate (%)",
    color = "Region",
    caption = "Source: FRED"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

The figure shows the monthly unemployment rate for all five regions on one set of axes.

## Unemployment rates by region (faceted)

```{r}
#| label: fig-facet
ggplot(unemp, aes(x = date, y = unemployment_rate, color = region)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~ region) +
  labs(
    title = "Regional Unemployment Rates Over Time",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Unemployment Rate (%)",
    caption = "Source: FRED"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

The same data as above, with a separate panel for each region so each region's path is easier to read.

## Average unemployment rate by region

```{r}
#| label: fig-bar
ggplot(unemp_summary, aes(x = fct_reorder(region, mean_rate), y = mean_rate)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    title = "Average Unemployment Rate by Region",
    x = "Region",
    y = "Mean Unemployment Rate (%)",
    caption = "Source: FRED, January 1976 to present"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Bars show each region's mean unemployment rate over the full sample, ordered from lowest to highest.

## Unemployment since 2015 with COVID marked

```{r}
#| label: fig-choice
ggplot(unemp_recent, aes(x = date, y = unemployment_rate, color = region)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = as.Date("2020-04-01"), linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    title = "Unemployment Rates Since 2015, April 2020 Marked",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Unemployment Rate (%)",
    color = "Region",
    caption = "Source: FRED. Dashed line marks April 2020."
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

I plotted unemployment rates since 2015 to look at COVID-related changes, with a dashed line at April 2020, when rates peaked. [EDIT: add one sentence about what you actually see, such as which regions spiked highest and how quickly they recovered.]

# 4. Reflection

My first errors came from running code before loading `tidyverse`, which made `mutate()` and `write_rds()` "not found," and from renaming a column that did not exist (the FRED value column is called `price`). Another stumbling block was that plots ran without errors but did not show up, which turned out to be a display and pane issue rather than a code problem.
